name: Klinkhammer
imitates: Hans van Klinken's emerger-style dry with a curved hook and parachute post; the abdomen hangs below the film like a hatching caddis or mayfly, and the post makes it easy to see.

steps.text: Secure the hook in the vise with the point and barb clear. Lock the thread in about a third of the shank behind the eye with a few wraps and trim the tag.
Run the thread forward in touching turns to behind the eye, then back to where the thread hangs just inside the hook bend.
Run the thread forward to about a quarter of the foundation behind the eye. Lay about four inches of poly yarn across the top of the shank and pin it with two or three pinch wraps.
Lift the front section of the yarn and wrap in front of the tie-in to make the post stand up, then wrap up the post to form a base for the hackle. Return the thread to the post base.
Pull the rear yarn tight and cut it at a taper, then cover it with touching thread wraps to shape the abdomen. Tie in the tip of the Krystal Flash rib and wrap back to the end of the foundation.
Dub a slender noodle on waxed thread and wrap it forward in touching turns over the abdomen, stopping just behind the post.
Counter-wrap the Krystal Flash rib in the opposite direction to the dubbing, in evenly spaced turns.
Strip the soft fibers from a hackle feather and tie it in against the post with the bright side inward, tip pointing down.
Dub the thorax in figure-eights around the post base, stopping just behind the eye.
Fold forward fibers back, form a small head, whip finish and trim the thread, then cement the head.
Turn the fly 90 degrees in the vise so the post is horizontal, lock the thread at the post base and wrap the hackle down the post without trapping fibers.
Pull the post tight and cut it just above the hackle, leaving roughly an eighth of an inch.
Whip finish slowly so no fibers are trapped, pull tight and cut the thread.
The finished Klinkhammer, ready for floatant on the post and hackle.
